_notes: The religious orders a diocese may hold a house of (requested in playtesting: a pastor may lean on a monastery). Each order rolls a house name from its list, an alignment around its mean, and a size; contemplatives pray for a parish, active houses send a confessor and a preacher. A diocese rolls one to four houses by size; every house is generated, none is a real one.

orders.label: the Benedictines
names: Our Lady of the Valley Abbey
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} who sing the hours and keep a guesthouse. They will pray for a parish that asks, and a pastor can send them his retreats.

orders.label: the Trappists
names: Our Lady of Good Counsel Abbey
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} an hour out of town, silent, with a bakery and a retreat house that is booked a year ahead.

orders.label: the Franciscans
names: Our Lady of the Angels Friary
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} in the city, who preach missions, run a kitchen, and hear confessions wherever they are asked.

orders.label: the Capuchins
orders.line: {name}, {size} bearded {members} of {order} with a soup line at the door and a confessional that is never empty.

orders.label: the Dominicans
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order}, preachers by trade, who will take a parish mission and a lecture series and argue with you at dinner.

orders.label: the Discalced Carmelites
names: Carmel of the Mother of God
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} behind a grille, who need a priest for Mass and pray for whoever sends one.

orders.label: the Poor Clares
names: Monastery of Our Lady of Light
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} on a side street, who take the parish's intentions on slips of paper and bake the altar breads.

orders.label: the Norbertines
names: Our Lady of the Assumption Abbey
orders.line: {name}, {size} {members} of {order} in white, who staff two parishes and a school and sing the Office in Latin every day of the year.
